data.name: v2.1.0
data.body:
## 2.1.0 (October 21, 2026)
BREAKING CHANGES:

* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Agent HTTP API request bodies are now limited to 512 KiB by default, including chunked requests and requests with an unsupported method, and oversized requests return HTTP 413 before the body is read in full. Very large `/v1/config` writes that previously succeeded can now fail. Raise the limit with the new `limits.http_max_request_body_size` setting if needed.
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Resource API (`/api/...`) request bodies are now subject to the same `limits.http_max_request_body_size` limit (512 KiB by default), and oversized requests return HTTP 413.
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** `GET /v1/agent/connect/ca/leaf/:service` now requires `service:write` on the requested service for every request, including requests served from the agent's cached leaf certificate. Requests with no token or a token without that permission now receive HTTP 403 instead of the cached certificate. Callers must present a token with `service:write` for the service.
* catalog: **(Enterprise only)** `Catalog.Register` now requires write permission on the node or service of an existing health check when updating it. Tokens that previously updated checks without that permission now receive a permission denied error.
* cli: Migrated the `consul connect redirect-traffic` command from `iptables`/`ip6tables` to `nftables` (`nft`). The command now uses the `sdk/nftables` package, which applies all IPv4 and IPv6 rules atomically in a single pass via the `nftables` `inet` address family, instead of separate `iptables` and `ip6tables` invocations. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* cli: Transparent proxy exclusions are now validated before rules are applied: user IDs must be numeric and outbound exclusions must be IP addresses or CIDRs. `iptables` previously also accepted user names, UID ranges, and host names. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* cli: `consul connect redirect-traffic` does not remove `iptables`/`ip6tables` rules created by earlier Consul versions. This only matters when upgrading an existing host or VM in place. Before running the new command on an existing host or VM, remove any Consul-managed `iptables` rules first (see the transparent proxy upgrade guide for a reference cleanup script). Leaving both rule sets in place can cause double NAT or inconsistent traffic redirection. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* docker: The official Consul container images now include `nftables` instead of `iptables`. Scripts that run `iptables` inside the Consul image must be updated. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* sdk: Replaced the `iptables` package with a new `nftables` package for transparent proxy traffic redirection. Traffic redirection now requires the `nft` binary and a Linux kernel with stateful NAT support in `nftables` `inet` family chains, available upstream starting with Linux kernel version 5.2 (some distributions backport this support onto an earlier nominal kernel version, for example RHEL 8+, kernel 4.18+, and its derivatives). There is no automatic fallback to `iptables`/`ip6tables`, so hosts without this kernel support will fail to set up transparent proxy redirection. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* feature-gates: Gate API Gateway HTTPRoute upstream-routing composition (PR #23294) behind the experimental feature `api-gateway-upstream-routing`. When disabled (default), the legacy HTTPRoute-to-router shape is preserved exactly. When enabled by an operator after a full datacenter upgrade, service-router rules are composed with HTTPRoute matches, resolver subset definitions are preserved, and discovery-chain watches use the correct HTTP protocol override. Existing agentless API Gateway proxy states are rebuilt automatically when the effective gate value changes.

SECURITY:

* Upgrade go version to 1.26.10 to address security vulnerabilities. [[GH-24067](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24067)]
* deps: upgrade `github.com/hashicorp/go-discover` to v1.5.0, removing the dependency on the archived `github.com/hashicorp/vic` module. This also upgrades `github.com/vmware/govmomi` to v0.55.1 and adds an `srv` provider for cloud auto-join. [[GH-24021](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24021)]
* security: **(Enterprise only)** Remove the `github.com/hashicorp/consul` root module dependency from the `test-integ` fault-injection tests to address [CVE-2026-15972](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15972) and [CVE-2026-88021](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-88021).
* security: Remove the `github.com/hashicorp/consul` root module dependency from the envoy integration test SDS server, the `consul-container` and `test-integ` test modules, and the `proto-gen-rpc-glue` e2e fixture to address [CVE-2026-15972](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15972). [[GH-24043](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24043)]
* deps: Upgrade github.com/hashicorp/raft-wal to v0.5.0 (with raft v1.8.0, serf v0.11.0, memberlist v0.7.0 and go-metrics v0.7.0), removing the dependency on github.com/coreos/etcd. [[GH-23985](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23985)]
* deps: Upgrade golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 to address GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6617 and GO-2026-6612. [[GH-23994](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23994)]
* docker: Run `apk upgrade` when building the Alpine-based container images so base-image packages (such as sqlite and jq) are up to date. [[GH-23964](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23964)]
* oauth: **(Enterprise only)** Avoid an unchecked size addition when merging JWKS key sets during OAuth key rotation.
* security: Upgrade github.com/klauspost/compress to v1.18.7, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to v1.17.10, github.com/moby/go-archive to v0.3.0 and github.com/go-openapi/swag to v0.27.1 to address CVE-2026-63209, CVE-2026-88031, CVE-2026-2303, CVE-2026-17106 and CVE-2026-85280. [[GH-23964](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23964)]
* ui: Add Content-Security-Policy header to Consul UI HTTP responses to mitigate XSS and data injection attacks. [[GH-23971](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23971)]
* ui: Pin a newer resolution of morgan to 1.12.1 to address GHSA-9f6g-j8ch-79g4 [[GH-23952](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23952)]
* Added debounce behavior to enforce a minimum interval between expensive federation-state anti-entropy sync operations. [[GH-23196](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23196)]
* Update `brace-expansion` to address [GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895) (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays). [[GH-23786](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23786)]
* Update `fast-uri` to address [GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7) (Host Confusion via backslash authority introducer). [[GH-23786](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23786)]
* Update `socket.io-parser` to address [CVE-2026-69185](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2m8v-j782-fhvr) (Zero-attachment Memory Exhaustion). [[GH-23786](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23786)]

FEATURES:

* acl: Add OIDC RP-Initiated IdP logout for tokens created via an `oidc` auth method: `consul logout` prints the identity provider's logout URL for the user to open (or opens it in the default browser with the new `-open-browser` flag or `CONSUL_LOGOUT_OPEN_BROWSER` environment variable), and the web UI opens it on logout, terminating the IdP session. Activates automatically when the IdP advertises an `end_session_endpoint` in its OIDC discovery document, or when the logout endpoint is configured explicitly with the new `OIDCLogoutURL` auth method setting for providers that do not advertise one. [[GH-23739](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23739)]
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Add an inline `ai` block to service definitions, letting a workload declare its AI role (`inference-model`, `mcp-server`, or `ai-agent`) and role-specific configuration in a single registration via config files and HTTP APIs. [[GH-13032](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13032)]
* api-gateway: Add `http2` and `grpc` as valid API Gateway listener protocols, enabling end-to-end HTTP/2 and gRPC from client to backend. Previously only `http` and `tcp` were accepted; the gateway would silently downgrade gRPC/HTTP2 traffic to HTTP/1.1 on the upstream hop. The new protocols render the correct downstream HTTP connection manager (HTTP/2 codec, `h2,http/1.1` ALPN) and align the upstream cluster to HTTP/2, closing the parity gap with Ingress Gateway. [[GH-23784](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23784)]
* api-gateway: Auto-register DNS for services exposed via an API Gateway, resolvable at `<service>.api-gateway.consul`. Populates the `gateway-services` catalog mapping for API Gateways and adds DNS SANs to the API Gateway Connect leaf certificate, bringing API Gateway to parity with Ingress Gateway. The feature is version-gated and backfills pre-existing gateways automatically once all servers are upgraded. [[GH-23647](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23647)]
* api-gateway: Support zero-touch downstream TLS termination. When `TLS { Enabled = true }` is set on an `api-gateway` config entry with no inline/file-system/SDS certificate, the gateway terminates downstream TLS using its Connect CA leaf certificate (with `*.api-gateway.consul` DNS SANs). Explicitly configured certificates continue to take precedence and are served as SNI overrides alongside the leaf default chain. [[GH-23647](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23647)]
* api-gateway: add `PassiveHealthCheck` to gateway-level default upstream limits and route service-level limit overrides, so passive health checking (Envoy outlier detection) can be configured for services routed through an API gateway. [[GH-23783](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23783)]
* cli: **(Enterprise only)** `consul connect envoy -gateway=inference` launches the policy processor alongside Envoy and enforces a minimum Envoy version for the inference gateway. The ext_proc socket is derived per proxy instance; `-ext-proc-socket-dir` overrides its directory (default `/var/run/consul`).
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Added an agent-managed OAuth client lifecycle for services with `ai.role` of `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`, including dynamic client registration with IBM Security Verify, key rotation, JWKS publication, and SDS delivery of the OAuth client credential to `ai-agent` Envoy sidecars.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Deliver OAuth sidecar credentials as AES-256-GCM envelopes. Content-encryption keys are persisted in KV and served via WorkloadKeyService.FetchKey so consul-obo-outbound can decrypt without becoming an SDS client.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Wire consul-obo-outbound and consul-obo-inbound ext_proc filters into connect-proxy xDS for hop-bound on-behalf-of token exchange.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Register services with `ai.role` of `ai-agent` or `mcp-server` with IBM Security Verify using `private_key_jwt`, persist DCR/JWKS in KV, and deliver the client credential to Envoy as SDS GenericSecret JSON for `ai-agent` workloads. Cluster IAM is an OIDC ACL auth method with `EnableServiceDCR=true` (agent `oauth.iam` HCL is rejected).
* connect: add `ecdh_curves` to `mesh` config entries (`MeshDirectionalTLSConfig`) and `tls_ecdh_curves` to agent TLS configuration (`TLSProtocolConfig`) to support configuring allowed ECDH/KEM curves for sidecar mTLS and agent RPC/HTTPS/gRPC, with automatic hybrid Post-Quantum `X25519MLKEM768` curve injection when `tls_min_version` is set to `TLSv1_3`. [[GH-23884](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23884)]
* feature-gates: Add Raft-backed dynamic feature gate framework (Phase 1). A new `feature_gates { bootstrap = { ... } }` server configuration block seeds the first Raft policy. The leader continuously reconciles desired policy, minimum-version eligibility, and registry defaults into a committed resolved status. Every server runs an atomic cache populated only from committed FSM state; agents consume an indexed resolved snapshot and fail closed until the first generation is delivered. New operator CLI commands `consul operator feature list`, `get`, and `set` provide CAS-safe, ACL-protected inspection and control of feature gates.
* operator: Add `GET /v1/operator/features`, `GET /v1/operator/feature/:name`, and `PUT /v1/operator/feature/:name` HTTP endpoints for reading and updating feature gate state. Reads require `operator:read`; writes require `operator:write`. All reads are blocking-query capable. [[GH-23791](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23791)]
* inference-gateway: **(Enterprise only)** Route opted-in external inference models through a terminating gateway. Models marked with the terminating-gateway egress are discovered from the catalog, resolved through the mesh discovery chain, and load-balanced across healthy terminating-gateway replicas, with capability-pool priority tiers and fail-closed behavior when no valid transport is available. A capability pool containing an external model is rejected, and its capability route returns 503, when two of its models render the same endpoint address or its model weights cannot be represented exactly.
* inference-gateway: **(Enterprise only)** Add the `inference-gateway` service kind and config entry. The gateway terminates inbound mesh mTLS, enforces intentions, and applies PII and routing policy through an ext_proc filter to a co-located policy processor. Model upstreams are services registered with `ai.role = "inference-model"` that intentions allow and that are reachable through the mesh (connect-enabled or behind a terminating gateway). The gateway connects to them over mTLS and selects them by capability, failing over across providers by priority.
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added server-side product usage metrics for ACL auth method counts (OIDC, Kubernetes, JWT) and audit logging config.
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added server-side product usage metrics for mesh gateway mode counts: `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_remote.count` and `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_local.count` report the number of service instances configured to use each mesh gateway mode, and `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_none.count` reports the number of service instances with no explicit mesh gateway mode (unset or `none`).
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added server-side product usage metrics for service intention default policy, service intention L7 and JWT counts
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added the server-side product usage metric `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_enabled`, which reports whether any mesh gateway instance is registered in the cluster. It is independent of the mesh gateway mode counts: those count connect-proxy sidecars by their upstream routing mode, while this reports whether the gateway capability is deployed at all.
* terminating-gateway: **(Enterprise only)** Add Vault-backed credential injection at the terminating gateway egress. A `TerminatingGateway` config entry now carries a `CredentialInjection` block (ext_proc processor UDS path and message timeout) and each linked service can declare a `Credential` binding (`Mode: "inject"` with a `BindingID`). At egress, an ext_proc filter calls a co-located processor that injects the bound credential (e.g. a provider API key sourced from Vault) into the upstream request, so credentials are never stored in mesh config or exposed to clients.
* xds: Add an inline "virtual DNS" UDP listener (127.0.0.1:8653) that serves an in-memory FQDN-to-VIP table derived from the proxy snapshot. It advertises VIPs for explicit upstreams, intention-allowed upstreams in transparent proxy mode, and cluster peering upstreams, while skipping cross-partition VIPs, stale/unauthorized discovery chains, and empty or non-IP entries so DNS responses stay in sync with what the transparent-proxy listener will actually intercept. Add an optional "egress DNS" UDP listener (127.0.0.1:8654) that forwards queries to agent-configured DNS recursors via c-ares when recursors are present. Extend the xDS `ConfigFetcher` interface (and agent implementation) to expose DNS recursors. [[GH-23698](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23698)]

IMPROVEMENTS:

* chore: Update of actions/cache/restore from 4.2.0 to 6.1.0
* chore: Update of actions/download-artifact from 4.1.7 to 8.0.2 [[GH-13634](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13634)]
* chore: Update of actions/upload-artifact from 4.3.3 to 7.0.2 [[GH-13635](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13635)]
* chore: Update of hashicorp/vault-action from 3 to 4 [[GH-13636](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13636)]
* connect: **(Enterprise Only)** update compatibility tests to Nomad ENT v1.9.13+ent, v1.10.17+ent, v1.11.11+ent, v2.0.7+ent and Vault ENT 1.19.22+ent, 1.20.16+ent, 1.21.11+ent, 2.0.4+ent, 2.1.1+ent and envoy 1.39.4, 1.38.7, 1.37.9, 1.36.13
* connect: revert the maximum supported Envoy version from 1.39.4 back to 1.39.1. Envoy 1.39.4 support, listed in a prior release note, is not included in this release. [[GH-24057](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24057)]
* connect: deliver the sidecar proxy's leaf certificate and CA roots to Envoy over SDS instead of embedding them inline in the public listener. Leaf certificate rotation is now a hitless hot-swap that no longer changes the listener filter chain hash, so established connections (notably long-lived TCP sessions) are no longer drained and terminated on every rotation. [[GH-23938](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23938)]
* terminating-gateway: deliver each linked service's Connect leaf certificate and the shared CA roots to Envoy over SDS instead of embedding them inline in the gateway's downstream filter chains. Leaf rotation no longer changes the filter chain hash, so established connections through the gateway are no longer drained. [[GH-23938](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23938)]
* api-gateway: add `invert` field to `HTTPHeaderMatch` in `http-route` config entries, enabling negated header match conditions (e.g. "route when header is absent" or "route when header value does NOT match"). Brings API Gateway to parity with the Ingress Gateway's existing `Invert` support in `service-router`. [[GH-23817](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23817)]
* ci: **(Enterprise only)** Increased the stale PR automation windows to 90 days before marking a pull request stale and 60 days before closing it. [[GH-13119](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13119)]
* peering: **(Enterprise only)** Add support for routing traffic to named ports on peered multiport services. [[GH-13142](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13142)]
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added three product usage metrics for auto-encrypt visibility. `consul.usage.client_agent_metric_included` reports whether client-agent metrics collection is enabled. `consul.usage.client_auto_encrypt_enabled.count` and `consul.usage.server_auto_encrypt_enabled.count` reports the number of clients and servers, respectively, with `auto_encrypt.tls` enabled. `consul.usage.auto_encrypt_enabled` combines both counts into a single boolean — true if auto-encrypt is enabled anywhere in the cluster be it client or server.
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added three server-side product usage metrics, `consul.usage.api_gateway.enabled` reports whether any API gateway instances are currently registered in the cluster, `consul.usage.mesh.service.percentage` reports the percentage of service instances that are connect-proxy sidecars and `consul.usage.transparent_proxy.enabled.percentage` reports the percentage of connect-proxy instances that have transparent proxy mode enabled.
* ui: Migrate the Consul UI to the HashiCorp Design System (HDS). This covers the global navigation shell and breadcrumbs, the list pages (key/value, peers, auth methods, services, service instances, nodes, intentions, linked services, upstreams, and access control), and the access control, namespace, and admin partition forms. Includes numerous accessibility (A11y) fixes. [[GH-23911](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23911)]
* xds: **(Enterprise only)** External inference-model upstreams are rendered with a destination-specific mTLS transport socket (per-model SDS validation context and SNI/SAN matching), so the gateway-to-model hop for terminating-gateway-fronted models is mutually authenticated and encrypted per model.
* xds: **(Enterprise only)** The `builtin/ext-proc` Envoy extension now supports Unix domain socket processor targets via `Target.Path`.

BUG FIXES:

* gateway: Fix a data race in the API gateway controller where the route reconciler kept adding to a `WatchSet` after handing it to a controller trigger that was already iterating it. The trigger is now registered only after all discovery chain reads are complete. [[GH-24018](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24018)]
* ui: Render tab content inside its tab panel so assistive technology can associate it with its tab, and keep focus on a tab after activating it [[GH-24013](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24013)]
* ui: Show errors loading a tab's content inside the page instead of as a second nested page [[GH-24013](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24013)]
* acl: **(Enterprise only)** Fixed Envoy escape-hatch key matching in `Proxy.Config` and per-upstream config so it follows the same case-folding rules as the config decoders. Keys that differ only by Unicode case folding (for example `envoy_local_cluſter_json`), and Go field-name forms such as `EnvoyListenerJSON`, now require `mesh:write` like their canonical spellings.
* agent: (Enterprise only) Fixed audit logging so request-body capture respects the body-size limit, uses the decoded request path when excluding KV bodies (for example `/v1/k%76/...`), and skips `/v1/txn` bodies. `POST /v1/operator/audit-hash` now returns HTTP 413 for oversized bodies.
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Fixed `PUT /v1/kv/` so chunked request bodies are bounded by `kv_max_value_size`, matching the existing `Content-Length` check.
* proxycfg: Fixed a goroutine and memory leak where a proxy's watches kept running after its state stopped unexpectedly, because replacing, deregistering or closing a stopped state did not cancel them. [[GH-23990](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23990)]
* proxycfg: Fixed a goroutine and memory leak where transparent proxies registered a new health watch for every imported peered service each time the imported services list changed, and never stopped watches for removed upstreams. [[GH-23990](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23990)]
* telemetry: Restore Raft, Serf, and Memberlist metrics in release artifacts by building with the `hashicorpmetrics` tag. [[GH-23813](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23813)]
* agent/xds: Fixed an issue where cross-cluster and peered requests originating from an API Gateway were rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden by downstream service RBAC intentions. Trailing semicolon-separated fields in the client certificate component of the `x-forwarded-client-cert` (XFCC) header (such as auto-registered DNS SANs) are now properly accepted by the RBAC principal regular expression. [[GH-23920](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23920)]
* cli: **(Enterprise only)** `consul intention create` now creates and replaces intentions via the exact (config-entry) intention API used by the UI, which supports non-default admin partitions (for example `-partition team-a`). Per-source metadata (`-meta`) continues to use the deprecated legacy intention API and is only supported in the default partition; combining `-meta` with a non-default partition now fails with a clear, actionable error. To attach metadata to intentions in an admin partition, use a `service-intentions` config entry with entry-level `Meta` via `consul config write`.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Attach outbound OBO only for identity-plane upstreams (`ai-agent` / `mcp-server`). Explicit HTTP upstreams to inference-gateway or inference-model destinations no longer get consul-obo-outbound and fail closed with "OBO audience not configured".
* connect: Fixed a bug where Consul servers ignored the configured `default_intention_policy` for three server-side surfaces — the intention check API (`consul intention check`, `GET /v1/connect/intentions/check`), the service topology view (`Internal.ServiceTopology`), and transparent proxy upstream discovery (`Internal.IntentionUpstreams`) — and fell back to `acl.default_policy` instead. This only changes behavior when `default_intention_policy` and `acl.default_policy` are set to opposite values; when they agree (or `default_intention_policy` is unset) there is no change. With `default_intention_policy=deny` and `acl.default_policy=allow`, the check API and topology previously reported connections as allowed even though they were denied; with `default_intention_policy=allow` and `acl.default_policy=deny`, transparent proxy sidecars under-provisioned their upstreams and could fail to reach services they were authorized to reach. Envoy RBAC enforcement was not affected and already honored `default_intention_policy`.

This release improves DNS caching, forwarding, and transport reliability,
with fixes for stale-cache handling, upstream connections, crashes/race fixes,
as well as enhancemence from quite a few plugins.

Forwarding now supports DNS-over-QUIC upstreams. Additional new features include
optional JSON query logging, authenticated RFC 2136 dynamic DNS updates, SIIT support,
expr-lang templates, and PROXY protocol v2 metadata.

The release is built with Go 1.27.3, covering CVE-2026-56865, CVE-2026-56864,
CVE-2026-33818, CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-97031, and CVE-2026-111943, along with

## Improvements

- Update background task records to omit original args and kwargs at creation, reducing unnecessary parameter persistence
- Strengthen persistent write protection for databases and Redis in high availability deployments across container restarts, recreation, and failure recovery
- Improve redeployment completion checks to tolerate normal replication lag, and refine switchover waits and recovery coordination to reduce false failure detection

## Bug Fixes

- Validate Access Token format while preserving fallback compatibility with other Bearer Token authentication methods
- Fix NLA configuration and RDP service refresh during Tinker applet host deployment, checking Group Policy and disabling listener NLA before installation, then verifying the configuration afterward; stop deployment with clear guidance when Group Policy requires NLA
- Fix race conditions involving role callbacks, operation locks, and file synchronization acknowledgments during switchover, automatic rejoin, and startup recovery [JumpServer EE]
- Improve MySQL/MariaDB replication position handling and crash recovery, and fix a race condition in PostgreSQL replication slot cleanup during standby rebuilds [JumpServer EE]
- Fix local administrator credential recovery and health checks during MySQL/MariaDB maintenance, avoiding the use of peer credentials or stale application passwords [JumpServer EE]

Declare user and group virtual provides for mysql and mysqlrouter on
openSUSE 16. Each package already creates its corresponding account

data.name: RabbitMQ 4.4.0
data.body:
RabbitMQ `4.4.0` is a new feature release.

## Breaking Changes and Compatibility Notes

 * The following AMQP 0-9-1 headers are no longer parsed:

   ```
   x-amqp-1.0-properties
   x-amqp-1.0-app-properties
   x-amqp-1.0-message-annotations
   x-amqp-1.0-footer
   ```

   RabbitMQ 3.13 and earlier used them to carry the AMQP 1.0 sections of a
   message received over AMQP 1.0. Nothing has written them since 4.0, so only
   a message stored by a 3.13 or earlier node and not read since carries them.
   Such a message is still delivered, with these headers converted like any
   other `x-` header rather than restored as AMQP 1.0 sections.

 * Likewise, the `x-basic-delivery-mode`, `x-basic-priority` and
   `x-basic-expiration` message annotations are no longer parsed. They were
   written before 4.0 when an AMQP 0-9-1 message was encoded as AMQP 1.0 for a
   stream, so only a stream entry written by a 3.13 or earlier node carries
   them, and reading it no longer restores those three properties.

 * OpenID Connect discovery responses are now validated more strictly. A
   deployment whose identity provider serves non-HTTPS (`http://`) endpoints,
   or whose `issuer` claim does not match the discovery endpoint used to
   retrieve it, will fail discovery validation after the upgrade.

   This is known to affect Cloud Foundry UAA, whose issuer is its token endpoint URL
   rather than a prefix of its discovery endpoint.

   Set `auth_oauth2.discovery.verify_issuer` and/or
   `auth_oauth2.discovery.verify_https_endpoints` to `false` before upgrading
   installations with non-compliant IdPs such as Cloud Foundry UAA.

   See [Discovery Payload Validation](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/oauth2#discovery-payload-validation)
   for details on validation rules and configuration options.

 * `GET /api/auth/hash_password/{password}` was replaced with another endpoint, `POST /api/auth/hash_password`.
    The new endpoint consumes a POST body with JSON document with one key `{"password": "..."}`


## Changes Worth Mentioning

### Core Server

#### Enhancements

 * This version fully supports Erlang 28 and 29 series for both new clusters
   and rolling upgrade scenarios.

 * Quorum queues now support delayed messages.

   A message with an `x-opt-delivery-time` annotation or header set to a future time,
   in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, is routed and enqueued immediately but only
   delivered to consumers once that time is reached.

   AMQP 1.0 clients set it as a message annotation, AMQP 0-9-1 clients as a
   `long` header.

   An AMQP 1.0 consumer can also delay redelivery of a message by setting
   `x-opt-delivery-time` in the annotations of a `modified` outcome.

   GitHub issue: [#16583](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16583)

 * AMQP 1.0 clients can now request sole (exclusive) ownership of a container ID.

   In case of a conflict, the server either refuses the new connection or closes the existing one,
   depending on what the client requested, per the [AMQP 1.0 Connection Uniqueness](https://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/soleconn/v1.0/soleconn-v1.0.html)
   protocol extension.

   GitHub issue: [#16669](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16669)

 * A new, optional `x-name-prefix` queue argument sets the prefix used for a server-named
   queue's generated name, capped at 64 bytes. The default prefix remains
   `amq.gen`.

   This feature is specific to AMQP 0-9-1.

   GitHub issue: [#16233](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16233)

 * The classic queue shared message store gained a new v2 on-disk file format (`.sqs`).
   New files are written in v2 automatically. Existing v1 files (`.rdq`) are left as-is.

   Note that a node with v2 files present cannot be downgraded to `4.3.x` or earlier.

   GitHub issue: [#17166](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17166)

 * Classic queues now perform compaction more efficiently.

   GitHub issue: [#16194](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16194)

 * `x-modulus-hash` exchange routing is now stable: assuming a topology that does not change,
   messages carrying the same routing key are now routed to the same bound destination.

   Note: the exchange type has been moved from `rabbitmq_sharding` to the core, so it is
   now available even when said plugin is not enabled.

   GitHub issue: [#15849](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/15849)

 * A change to the `delivery-limit` policy key now takes effect for existing quorum queues.

   Previously the delivery limit could not be updated from a policy. Now quorum queues
   reconfigure their `delivery-limit` value when a policy is added or updated.

   When the policy is removed the queue goes back to the default limit (`20`).

   A negative policy value means "no limit".

   GitHub issue: [#16035](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16035)

 * A passive declaration of a queue or an exchange (a check that it exists) requires any one of
   the `configure`, `write` or `read` permissions on that queue or exchange.

   This applies to `queue.declare` and `exchange.declare` with `passive` set to `true` in
   AMQP 0-9-1, and to queue lookups in AMQP 1.0 management.

   GitHub issue: [#16272](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16272)

 * Reduce boot time of blank (brand new) nodes.

   GitHub issue: [#16479](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16479)

 * [Encrypted value](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/configure#configuration-encryption) support
   for the `definitions.https.url` key in `rabbitmq.conf`.

   GitHub issue: [#16632](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16632)

 * Password salts for internal users are now generated using a cryptographically secure
   pseudorandom number generator (CPRNG).

   GitHub issue: [#16775](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16775)

 * A topic exchange binding key can now contain at most two multi-segment (`#`) wildcards.

   GitHub issue: [#17039](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17039)

 * Redeclaring a stream with an `x-max-age` value that is equal to the existing one but written in
   different units, for example `1D` as `24h`, is no longer rejected as having non-equivalent arguments.

   GitHub issues: [#8509](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/8509), [#17259](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17259)

 * A stream can now start at an offset other than `0`, set with the new
   `x-stream-initial-offset` optional queue argument. While the stream is empty,
   the `first` and `next` offset specifications resolve to this offset. The stream
   protocol accepts the same value as the `stream-initial-offset` argument of the
   `Create` command.

   The initial offset is fixed when the stream is created, so there is no policy
   for it, and redeclaring the stream with a different value is rejected.

   GitHub issue: [#17300](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17300)

 * Multiple stream coordinator efficiency improvements.

   For example, the stream coordinator now retries failed stream member actions sooner, with
   keeping a related stream partition process blocked for the retry delay.

   Failed operations are now retried after a short randomised delay, and actions that
   failed because a node was down are retried when that node comes back.

   GitHub issue: [#16515](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16515)

 * Certain classic queue recovery scenarios now avoid a counterproductive timeout of 60s.

   GitHub issue: [#17733](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17733)

 * Reduce CPU use of mostly idle quorum queues that do not have any queue decorators configured
   (which is the common, baseline case).

   GitHub issues: [#17702](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/17702), [#17758](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17758)

 * PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 now can be used for password hashing:

   ```ini
   password_hashing_module = rabbit_password_hashing_pbkdf2_sha256
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#17316](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17316)

 * AMQP listeners can now bind to a Unix domain socket, using the same `listeners.tcp.*`
   settings as a TCP listener:

   ```ini
   listeners.tcp.1 = unix:/var/run/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.sock:0
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#16963](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16963)

 * `connection_max` and `channel_max` were renamed to `max_connections` and `max_channels`,
   respectively, in `rabbitmq.conf`. The original names are still supported.

   GitHub issue: [#16347](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16347)

 * Messages are now converted from AMQP 0-9-1 to
   AMQP 1.0 as a single data section, unless its payload consists of valid AMQP 1.0 body sections.

   An `expiration` value that cannot be parsed is now ignored during that conversion.

   GitHub issue: [#17272](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17272)

 * Client connection listener startup now can be delayed by a configurable number of seconds
   (default: no additional delay):

   ```ini
   listeners.startup_delay = 10
   ```

   GitHub issues: [#13153](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/13153), [#17289](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17289)

 * Internal peer discovery improvements.

   GitHub issue: [#17450](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17450)

#### Bug Fixes

 * The stream coordinator could leave a stream without a writer and never recover it,
   keep a stale `start` action after a leader election, or leave a replica
   disconnected after its node came back.

   GitHub issue: [#16515](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16515)

 * Multiple bug fixes and optimizations to Single Active Consumers on streams.

   GitHub issues: [#15695](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/15695), [#16515](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16515), [#16976](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16976)

 * AMQP 1.0: link handle uniqueness is now enforced per the protocol spec.

   GitHub issue: [#15780](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/15780)

 * Fix an issue that could trip an upgrade from `3.13` to `4.2` and then immediately to `4.3`.

   GitHub issue: [#16990](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16990)

 * Upgrade safety improvements in mixed-version clusters (during rolling upgrades).

   GitHub issue: [#17128](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17128)

 * Several bug fixes around binding deletion.

   GitHub issues: [#17255](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/17255), [#17257](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17257)

 * Quorum queue [Continuous Membership Reconciliation](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/quorum-queues#member-reconciliation) (CMR)
   could add more members (replicas) than the configured limit.

   GitHub issues: [#17310](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/17310), [#17311](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17311)

 * Fixed an off-by-one issue in classic queue shared message store after an unclean shutdown.

   GitHub issue: [#17351](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17351)

 * Routing to queues now handles concurrent queue deletion gracefully in more places, avoiding
   confusing (and also non-actionable) exceptions.

   GitHub issue: [#17664](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17664)

 * The `basic.cancel` notification sent on a [consumer delivery timeout](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/consumers#acknowledgement-timeout)
   now properly clears consumer state even if the client does not respond with `basic.cancel-ok`.

   GitHub issue: [#17734](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17734)


### CLI Tools

#### Enhancements

 * Two new commands, `rabbitmqctl sole_connection_status` and
   `rabbitmqctl sole_connection_force_delete`, inspect and manage AMQP 1.0 sole connections.

   GitHub issue: [#16669](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16669)

 * CLI commands that accept sensitive values as interactive input now suppress terminal echoing
   where possible. This behavior is specific to Erlang 28 and 29.

   GitHub issue: [#17585](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17585)


### Stream Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * `stream.max_connections` is a new `rabbitmq.conf` setting that limits the concurrent
   number of RabbitMQ Stream Protocol client connections.

   GitHub issue: [#16347](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16347)

 * `stream.max_super_stream_partitions` is a new `rabbitmq.conf` setting that limits the number of
   partitions a super stream can have.

   GitHub issue: [#16689](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16689)

### Management Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * A new endpoint, `GET /api/init`, cuts the number of blocking requests the UI
   has to make with certain authentication and login flows.

   GitHub issue: [#17287](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17287)

 * The `Referrer-Policy` response header value of the HTTP API and the UI can now be configured
   using the `management.headers.referrer_policy` key.

   GitHub issue: [#16893](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16893)

 * Support for multiple listeners for all HTTP-based protocols and the HTTP API.

   GitHub issues: [#11526](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/11526), [#17365](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17365)

#### Bug Fixes

 * The HTTP API did not return the status of blocked consumers.

   GitHub issue: [#16532](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16532)

### MQTT Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * `mqtt.max_connections` is a new `rabbitmq.conf` setting that limits the concurrent
   number of MQTT client connections.

   GitHub issue: [#16367](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16367)

 * MQTT 5.0: a `Receive Maximum` value of `0` is now rejected per the protocol spec.

   GitHub issue: [#17057](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17057)

 * The MQTT retained message store now has per-virtual host limits on the number of retained
   messages and their total size. A message that would exceed either limit is not retained.

   The defaults are 100,000 messages and 1 GiB. Both can be changed, or set to `infinity`:

   ```ini
   mqtt.retained_message_store.max_messages = 100000
   mqtt.retained_message_store.max_size_bytes = 1073741824
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#17189](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17189)

### STOMP Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * Following the footsteps of AMQP 1.0 and MQTT in previous years,
   the STOMP is now a standardlone protocol, that is, it is no longer built on AMQP 0-9-1.

   GitHub issue: [#9141](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/9141)

 * * `stomp.max_connections` is a new `rabbitmq.conf` setting that limits the concurrent
   number of STOMP client connections.

   GitHub issue: [#16368](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16368)


### Web MQTT Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * The `Strict-Transport-Security` (HSTS) header value can now be configured
   using the `web_mqtt.hsts.policy` key:

   ```ini
   web_mqtt.hsts.policy = max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#16772](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16772)

 * A new `web_mqtt.strict_origin_validation` configuration key makes the plugin reject a WebSocket upgrade
   request without an `Origin` header when `web_mqtt.allow_origins` restricts the allowed origins.

   `web_mqtt.allow_origins` also accepts a new value, `same_origin`, which only allows requests whose
   `Origin` matches the origin of the request itself:

   ```ini
   web_mqtt.allow_origins = same_origin
   web_mqtt.strict_origin_validation = true
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#16813](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16813)

### Web STOMP Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * The `Strict-Transport-Security` (HSTS) header value can now be configured
   using the `web_stomp.hsts.policy` key:

   ```ini
   web_stomp.hsts.policy = max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#16772](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16772)

 * A new `web_stomp.strict_origin_validation` configuration key makes the plugin reject a WebSocket upgrade
   request without an `Origin` header when `web_stomp.allow_origins` restricts the allowed origins.

   `web_stomp.allow_origins` also accepts a new value, `same_origin`, which only allows requests whose
   `Origin` matches the origin of the request itself:

   ```ini
   web_stomp.allow_origins = same_origin
   web_stomp.strict_origin_validation = true
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#16813](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16813)

### Auth Backend OAuth 2 Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * OpenID Connect discovery responses fetched from identity providers are now
   validated according to OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 spec seciton §4.3. See
   [Discovery Payload Validation](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/oauth2#discovery-payload-validation)
   for details on validation rules and configuration options.

   GitHub issue: [#17363](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17363)

 * OAuth 2.0 scopes now ca be extracted using regular expressions.

   GitHub issue: [#16196](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16196)

### Auth Backend Cache Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * The cache was never hit when the same user reconnected with the same credentials.

   On busy deployments this could put significant extra load on the upstream authentication
   backend and its dependencies, for example, the LDAP backend and the LDAP server(s) it uses.

   GitHub issues: [#16255](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/16255), [#16258](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16258)

### Consistent Hashing Exchange Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Routing no longer fails when the header it hashes on holds an empty array.

   GitHub issue: [#17081](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17081)

### Federation Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Under certain conditions, deleting a federated queue could modify an exchange with the same
   name in the same virtual host.

   GitHub issues: [#16991](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/16991), [#16997](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16997)

### Shovel Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Deleting a shovel that was still in the `starting` state left its status behind instead of deleting it.

   GitHub issue: [#16767](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/16767)

 * A local shovel with `src-delete-after` set could transfer more messages than the configured number.

   GitHub issue: [#17209](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17209)

 * When the destination rejects a message, for example because the destination queue
   has `x-overflow` set to `reject-publish` and has reached its maximum length, the shovel
   now returns the message to the source queue as a failed delivery. A quorum source queue
   therefore dead-letters the message once it exceeds the [delivery limit](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/quorum-queues#poison-message-handling),
   instead of redelivering it to the shovel over and over (a regression in `4.3.0`).

   With an AMQP 1.0 source, such a message used to be dead-lettered on the first rejection.
   Now this happens once it exceeds the delivery limit. A classic source queue has no
   delivery limit, so the message is returned to it until the destination accepts it.

   GitHub issue: [#17794](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17794)

 * A shovel with an AMQP 1.0 destination did not settle a message at the source when
   the destination rejected or released it, and eventually stopped forwarding messages.

   GitHub issue: [#17794](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17794)

 * A shovel with an AMQP 1.0 source could restart and forward some messages twice when
   the destination confirmed messages out of order.

   GitHub issue: [#17794](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17794)

 * A shovel with an AMQP 1.0 source could settle messages incorrectly after more than
   4 billion deliveries. With a local destination, it could acknowledge a message at the
   source before the destination confirmed it.

   GitHub issue: [#17794](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17794)

### Erlang AMQP 0-9-1 Client

#### Enhancements

 * The `auth_mechanism` query parameter of an AMQP 0-9-1 URI is now restricted to
   the mechanisms the client actually supports (`plain`, `amqplain`, `external`,
   `crdemo`), and an unsupported value is now rejected when the URI is parsed
   rather than when the connection is established. This also applies to the
   Shovel and federation plugins, which parse URIs the same way.

 * Likewise, the `verify` query parameter of an AMQP 0-9-1 URI now only accepts
   `verify_peer` or `verify_none`, and an unsupported value is rejected when the
   URI is parsed rather than when the TLS connection is established.

### Erlang AMQP 1.0 Client

#### Enhancements

 * Connection configuration now accepts a `connect_timeout`, applied to the socket
   connect and, for TLS, to the handshake as well. Without it, a peer that accepts the
   TCP connection and then stops responding blocks `amqp10_client_sup` indefinitely,
   which in turn blocks every other connection attempt in the node.
   Defaults are unchanged: `infinity` for TCP and TLS, 5000 ms for WebSockets.

### Dependency Changes

 * `osiris` was upgraded to [`1.14.1`](https://github.com/rabbitmq/osiris/releases)
 * `ra` was upgraded to [`3.2.0`](https://github.com/rabbitmq/ra/releases)
 * `khepri` was upgraded to [`0.19.3`](https://github.com/rabbitmq/khepri/releases/tag/v0.19.3)
 * [`portunus`](https://github.com/rabbitmq/portunus) was introduced at [`0.14.0`](https://github.com/rabbitmq/portunus/releases/tag/v0.14.0)
 * `thoas` was dropped: JSON encoding and decoding now uses the Erlang/OTP `json` module

## Source Code Archives

To obtain source code of the entire distribution, please download the archive named `rabbitmq-server-4.4.0.tar.xz`
instead of the source tarball produced by GitHub.

data.body:
Helm v4.3.1 is a patch release. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

The community keeps growing, and we'd love to see you there!

- Join the discussion in [Kubernetes Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com):
  -  for questions and just to hang out
  -  for discussing PRs, code, and bugs
- Hang out at the Public Developer Call: Thursday, 9:30 Pacific via [Zoom](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meeting/91295593969?password=17825db5-c698-44cc-9f00-ef1f61f5d3fb)
- Test, debug, and contribute charts: [ArtifactHub/packages](https://artifacthub.io/packages/search?kind=0)

## Notable Changes

- fix(action): wait for CRD establishment under HookOnlyStrategy #32672 by @pujitha24
- fix(linters): update golangci-lint to v2.14.0 #32744 by @ruslan-shaydullin 

## Installation and Upgrading

Download Helm v4.3.1. The common platform binaries are here:

- [MacOS amd64](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-darwin-amd64.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-darwin-amd64.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 34bec4eba761ba5c16d1965ee6b8f5b0abe5993974a802274e2a4f0418893d89)
- [MacOS arm64](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 6b4e61c8cd27d99e5a801e63ff25dd5c70b36875c2cd659d3e9ce6b76fc23198)
- [Linux amd64](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-amd64.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-amd64.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 0403a88ae20913d11b10a2467b50087721fea7581736da6b9d3992f5357fe54b)
- [Linux arm](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-arm.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-arm.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 292588ea9f89705511c93a39687fe5e26767bd85b5085a1be9a2a1563c1e28fa)
- [Linux arm64](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-arm64.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-arm64.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 8cf8f66ecbc252ac8f7f06cca68aba88508ddfde3a6a34feb1678ad1694b4f88)
- [Linux i386](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-386.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-386.tar.gz.sha256sum) / bfe8cbbec02362d869e183f27ca03342820ceae908f7a7db2e17caeef74e6d30)
- [Linux loong64](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-loong64.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-loong64.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 5fc8ae4eb1d513775374160a1ff5255290b86e8a71beeae09ae7d3a60f50962f)

- [Linux s390x](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-s390x.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.1-linux-s390x.tar.gz.sha256sum) / dfb031400c1215c0bd673d5e25bcd300a5af903fbfed10b5cb8b3ffc03bcecb6)

This release was signed with `208D D36E D5BB 3745 A167 43A4 C7C6 FBB5 B91C 1155` and can be found at @scottrigby [keybase account](https://keybase.io/r6by). Please use the attached signatures for verifying this release using `gpg`.

The [Quickstart Guide](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/quickstart/) will get you going from there. For **upgrade instructions** or detailed installation notes, check the [install guide](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/). You can also use a [script to install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-4) on any system with `bash`.

## What's Next

- 4.3.2 and 3.22.2 are the next patch releases scheduled for November 11, 2026
- 4.4.0 is the next minor release scheduled for January 13, 2027. There will be no further Helm 3 minor releases (see https://helm.sh/blog/helm-v3-end-of-life)

## Changelog

- chore(deps): bump otlploghttp and stdoutlog to v0.21.0 c0d08d0d6d9424d4a14febb5e8a3e51b0dd00dff (Terry Howe)
- chore(deps): bump the k8s-io group across 1 directory with 7 updates 0c0146eb409bcbc1793d97d67500cdf55050a742 (dependabot[bot])

Welcome to the v2.4.2 release of containerd! The second patch release for containerd 2.4 contains various fixes and updates including security patches. ### Security Updates * **containerd** * [**CVE-2026-95839**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-vwhp-8p66-mq4f) * [**GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc) * [**GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66) ### Highlights #### Container Runtime Interface (CRI) * Apply hardening to not follow symlinks for container log files ([#14302](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14302)) #### Image Distribution * Fix excessive memory usage during image pulls when registry downloads outpace content writes ([#14342](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14342)) * Apply hardening to reject image references with ".." path components ([#14282](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14282)) #### Runtime * Apply hardening to allowlist socket domains in the default seccomp profile ([#14247](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14247)) Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues. ### Contributors * Samuel Karp * Maksym Pavlenko * Sebastiaan van Stijn * Derek McGowan * LEI WANG * Paweł Gronowski * Phil Estes * Wei Fu * syed abdul khaliq ### Changes

data.name: Vitess v24.0.5
data.body:
# Release of Vitess v24.0.5

## Summary

### Unsupported `sql_mode` values are rejected

#### VTGate

VTGate already rejected `SET sql_mode = ...` statements that enable a mode the Vitess parser does not support (`ANSI_QUOTES`, `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`, `PIPES_AS_CONCAT`, `REAL_AS_FLOAT`). The check compared mode names textually and could be bypassed. VTGate now implements MySQL 8.x's `sql_mode` assignment semantics and validates every assignment against them:

- Setting an unsupported mode is rejected even when the underlying MySQL already runs with that mode, that is, when the `SET` would not change the value. Such statements previously succeeded, even though VTGate does not parse queries under these modes. The combination mode `ANSI` is rejected as well, because it enables `ANSI_QUOTES`, `PIPES_AS_CONCAT`, and `REAL_AS_FLOAT`.
- `IGNORE_SPACE` and `HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE` are now also rejected. They are the two remaining modes that change how SQL text is interpreted. The Vitess parser does not honor them, so VTGate would parse queries differently than the session's `sql_mode` promises.
- Unknown mode names and invalid numeric values fail with MySQL's own errors: `ER_WRONG_VALUE_FOR_VAR` (1231), and `ER_UNSUPPORTED_SQL_MODE` (3899) for the bits of modes removed in MySQL 8.0.
- Numeric values decode against MySQL's `sql_mode` bitmask. For example, `SET sql_mode = 1048576` reports that `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` is unsupported. Valid numeric values are accepted.
- Constant values are validated at planning time, with no shard round trip. This includes constant expressions such as `CONCAT` over literals, and it also applies when `--enable-system-settings` is disabled. Non-constant expressions are validated at execution time, once their value is known.

#### VTTablet

VTTablet applies the same validation at its own entry points and returns the same errors: connection settings, on the settings pool and on reserved connections, and session-scope `SET sql_mode` statements. This covers clients that bypass VTGate's validation, such as VTGates that are not upgraded yet and clients that talk to the query service directly. `SET_VAR` optimizer hints are forwarded to MySQL unchanged.

Every MySQL connection Vitess creates now strips the modes that change how SQL text is interpreted from the session `sql_mode` it inherits from the server's global value. All other modes, such as the strict modes and the zero-date modes, are kept. This applies to every component: query serving, schema tracking, heartbeats, replication management, Online DDL, VReplication and VDiff, and connections to external MySQL servers. The global `sql_mode` is not changed.

#### Impact

- Clients that run `SET sql_mode` with an unsupported mode, including `ANSI`, `IGNORE_SPACE` and `HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE`, now receive an error. This also happens when the `SET` matches the backend's current `sql_mode`. Clients that set mode names MySQL would itself reject receive an error as well.
- During a rolling upgrade, VTTablets are typically upgraded before VTGates. A session that sets a now-rejected `sql_mode` through a VTGate that is not upgraded yet starts receiving errors from upgraded VTTablets.
- A backend whose global `sql_mode` includes one of these modes keeps it, but Vitess sessions no longer inherit it.

See [#20883](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/20883) for details.

### Table ACL: callers with every role on every table may run statements whose tables cannot be determined

v24.0.4 began denying, under strict table ACL (`--queryserver-config-strict-table-acl`), statements whose tables vttablet cannot determine (`DO`, `CALL`, `REPAIR`, `OPTIMIZE`, `LOAD DATA`, and a `CREATE TABLE` that vttablet's parser cannot fully parse) for every caller outside the exempt ACL (`--queryserver-config-acl-exempt-acl`); see [GHSA-w6mx-2f8x-pqf4](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-w6mx-2f8x-pqf4). A caller that is a reader, a writer and an admin in a table group covering every table (`"table_names_or_prefixes": ["%"]`) holds every role on any table such a statement could touch, so `DO`, `REPAIR`, `OPTIMIZE` and a partially parsed `CREATE TABLE` now run for it. `CALL` and `LOAD DATA` remain denied even then, since a `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` procedure runs with its definer's privileges and `LOAD DATA INFILE` reads files on the server, neither of which table ACL grants; issue them as a caller in the exempt ACL.

These checks are counted under the `undetermined-table-set` `TableName` label, in `TableACLDenied`, or in `TableACLAllowed` for a caller with every role on every table. With dry-run (`--queryserver-config-enable-table-acl-dry-run`), only the statements the check would deny increment `TableACLPseudoDenied`.

See [#21349](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21349) for details.

### Connection character sets restricted

`--db-charset`, and the other places a MySQL connection character set is configured, no longer accept `sjis`, `cp932`, `gb18030`, `gbk`, `big5`, `ucs2`, `utf16`, `utf16le` or `utf32`, whether given as a character set or as one of its collations. A tablet configured with one of them fails to start, VTGate refuses a `SET` of `character_set_client`, `character_set_connection`, `character_set_results` or `collation_connection` to one of them, or to a name that is not a character set or collation, which it used to answer with OK and ignore, and VTTablet refuses a setting or `SET` statement that would switch a session's connection to one of them. A client may still ask for one of them at the handshake: VTGate reads its statements byte by byte, as the tablet's connection to MySQL does, so they cannot break out of a literal.

Vitess parses and escapes SQL text byte by byte, and in these character sets the second byte of a character can be a backslash or a back quote, so text in them was misparsed or corrupted on its way through Vitess. Use `utf8mb4` as the connection character set instead. Tables and columns can still be declared with any of these character sets; MySQL converts between them and the connection character set.

This fixes [GHSA-c28j-qmfx-4gxp](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-c28j-qmfx-4gxp).

See [#21392](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21392) and [#21465](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21465) for details.

### Charset and collation names are quoted when regenerated

A charset, collation, engine, tablespace or full-text parser name is now decoded when parsed, and written back as a single token when Vitess regenerates the statement: bare when it is a known charset, collation, engine, index type or parser name, back-quoted otherwise.

User-visible consequences:

- **A quoted name is normalized.** `COLLATE 'utf8_bin'` regenerates as `COLLATE utf8_bin` — the quoted and unquoted spellings mean the same name, and the decoded form is what is stored. Anything comparing the printed form of these statements byte for byte sees the new spelling.
- **Only known names stay bare.** A charset or collation name of any MySQL or MariaDB version, a known storage engine such as `InnoDB` or `memory`, the `BTREE`, `HASH` and `RTREE` index types, the `ngram` and `mecab` parsers, and the `innodb_system` and `innodb_file_per_table` tablespaces are written back as they were spelled. Any other name is back-quoted: `TABLESPACE ts` regenerates as ``TABLESPACE `ts` ``, and so does an engine Vitess does not know or a keyword used as a name. `WITH PARSER` accepts only a plain identifier, so a known name that is a keyword is quoted there: ``WITH PARSER `memory` `` keeps its quoting where `ENGINE memory` does not. `binary` is still bare where the grammar has a `BINARY` alternative, except directly before the `BINARY` attribute: `CHARACTER SET 'binary' BINARY` regenerates as ``CHARACTER SET `binary` BINARY``.
- **`COLLATE binary` in an expression is quoted.** `expr COLLATE binary` regenerates as ``expr COLLATE `binary` ``, because MySQL's expression `COLLATE` only accepts `binary` quoted. Column, table and database `COLLATE binary` and `CHARACTER SET binary` stay bare.
- **An empty charset, collation, engine or partition tablespace name is rejected.** `CHARACTER SET ''` and `COLLATE ''` on a column, a table, `ALTER TABLE ... CONVERT TO`, `CAST`/`CONVERT`, `CONVERT ... USING`, `CHAR ... USING`, `SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE` and an expression, `ENGINE ''` on a table or a partition, and a partition's `TABLESPACE ''` no longer parse. An empty name in these positions is indistinguishable from the clause being absent, so it would previously have been dropped or mangled and a statement MySQL rejects could have become a valid, different one. Non-DDL statements get the error directly; DDL falls back to a partial parse, so the client's own text is forwarded and MySQL rejects it. `SET NAMES ... COLLATE ''` and `SET CHARACTER SET ... COLLATE ''`, which used to parse and discard the collation, are now parse errors too; MySQL rejects both. `CREATE`/`ALTER DATABASE ... CHARACTER SET ''` and `COLLATE ''` are unchanged: they still parse and are written back as `''`.
- **`ENCRYPTION` requires a quoted value.** `CREATE`/`ALTER DATABASE ... ENCRYPTION N` no longer fully parses, matching MySQL, which only accepts `'Y'` or `'N'` as a quoted string. Such a statement now falls back to a partial parse rather than being regenerated into a spelling MySQL would refuse.

This fixes [GHSA-j8pc-mcwq-qrg6](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-j8pc-mcwq-qrg6).

See [#21435](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21435) for details.

### VTAdmin VExplain modes that run the statement require the `execute` action

VTAdmin's VExplain API was authorized with the `get` action, but `VEXPLAIN QUERIES`, `ALL` and `TRACE` run the statement they explain, so an actor allowed only to read could change data through it ([GHSA-c2r8-grjp-w8c2](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-c2r8-grjp-w8c2)). Those modes now require the new `execute` action on the `VExplain` resource; `PLAN` and `KEYS`, which only plan the statement, still require only `get`. For those modes VTAdmin also accepts only a `SELECT` without `INTO`, sequence next-values or advisory lock functions, and runs them in a read-only transaction that is always rolled back. The VExplain page in the web UI now defaults to `PLAN`.

**Migration**: grant the `execute` action on `VExplain` to the actors that should run `VEXPLAIN QUERIES`, `ALL` or `TRACE`. Rules that grant all actions (`*`) and `--no-rbac` already include it.

**Impact**: an actor with only `get` on `VExplain` gets an `unauthorized` error from `VEXPLAIN QUERIES`, `ALL` and `TRACE`.

See [#21396](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21396) for details.

### Security fixes

- Fixes [GHSA-73pp-99vw-h5g8](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-73pp-99vw-h5g8): SQL injection through VStream LastPK values. See [#21377](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21377).
- Fixes [GHSA-92cc-q2h6-m2vr](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-92cc-q2h6-m2vr): SQL injection through `convert_tz()` arguments in a VStream filter. See [#21377](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21377).
- Fixes [GHSA-8w3p-4xg5-rm9w](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-8w3p-4xg5-rm9w): SQL injection through table names in Online DDL statements. See [#21381](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21381).
- Fixes [GHSA-x56j-8c72-5xgg](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-x56j-8c72-5xgg): SQL injection through the caller ID in query annotations (`--queryserver-config-annotate-queries`). See [#21369](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21369).
- Fixes [GHSA-m282-7w35-g77m](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-m282-7w35-g77m): SQL injection through a global `SET` variable name. See [#21390](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21390).
- Fixes [GHSA-9248-hccp-qf8f](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-9248-hccp-qf8f): SQL injection through `DATE`, `TIME` and `TIMESTAMP` literals. See [#21389](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21389).
- Fixes [GHSA-9rx3-8pwm-c228](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-9rx3-8pwm-c228): SQL injection through a session variable value carried in a `SET_VAR` hint. See [#21388](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21388).
- Fixes [GHSA-pfg5-ppc7-ff45](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-pfg5-ppc7-ff45): SQL hidden from parsing and table ACL checks in a trailing comment. See [#21387](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21387).
- Fixes [GHSA-xf67-9r78-xv82](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-xf67-9r78-xv82): SQL injection through malformed numeric bind variables. See [#21386](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21386).
- Fixes [GHSA-3fr2-mqr5-r5x5](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-3fr2-mqr5-r5x5): VTAdmin API routes that change cluster state accepted cross-site `GET` requests. See [#21397](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21397).
- Fixes [GHSA-78h7-x6qm-xpr8](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/security/advisories/GHSA-78h7-x6qm-xpr8): VTAdmin's `ReloadSchemaShard` did not check RBAC. See [#21394](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/21394).

------------
The entire changelog for this release can be found [here](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/blob/main/changelog/24.0/24.0.5/changelog.md).

The release includes 30 merged Pull Requests.

Thanks to all our contributors: @app/vitess-bot, @arthurschreiber, @lmorduch, @mattlord
Stamp 19rc1.

data.name: v4.6.2
data.body:
# OpenEBS 4.6.2 Release Notes

## Release Summary
OpenEBS v4.6.2 is a patch release on top of v4.6.1, delivering targeted fixes and minor enhancements across the Helm chart and the storage engines. It fixes image pulls for the MinIO pods that serve as Loki's object store, a backup and restore hang in Local PV ZFS, and failing operations on Local PV Rawfile volumes created before storage pools were introduced.

This release includes new patch releases of Replicated PV Mayastor (v2.12.2), Local PV ZFS (v2.11.2) and Local PV Rawfile (v0.15.3). Local PV LVM remains at v1.10.1 and Local PV Hostpath remains at v4.6.0.

v4.6.2 includes all changes from [v4.6.0](https://github.com/openebs/openebs/releases/tag/v4.6.0) and [v4.6.1](https://github.com/openebs/openebs/releases/tag/v4.6.1). See those release notes for the features and fixes in the 4.6 line.

Upgrading is recommended for:
- Anyone on v4.3.0 through v4.6.1 running the chart's default Loki and MinIO setup.
- Local PV ZFS users on v4.6.0 or v4.6.1 who back up volumes with Velero.
- Local PV Rawfile users with volumes created before storage pools were introduced, for example with v4.4.0.

## Engine Versions

| Engine | Version | Release Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Replicated PV Mayastor | v2.12.2 | [Mayastor v2.12.2 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/mayastor/releases/tag/v2.12.2) |
| Local PV ZFS | v2.11.2 | [Local PV ZFS v2.11.2 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/zfs-localpv/releases/tag/v2.11.2) |
| Local PV LVM | v1.10.1 | [Local PV LVM v1.10.1 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/lvm-localpv/releases/tag/v1.10.1) |
| Local PV Hostpath | v4.6.0 | [Local PV Hostpath v4.6.0 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/dynamic-localpv-provisioner/releases/tag/v4.6.0) |
| Local PV Rawfile | v0.15.3 | [Local PV Rawfile v0.15.3 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/releases/tag/v0.15.3), [v0.15.2 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/releases/tag/v0.15.2) |

## Change Summary
## General
- Switch the OpenEBS chart's Loki MinIO images to an OpenEBS mirror on Docker Hub (`docker.io/openebs/minio` and `docker.io/openebs/mc`), keeping the same image tags. v4.3.0 through v4.6.1 pull the `minio` and `mc` images from `quay.io/minio`, which can no longer be pulled anonymously, so MinIO pods can fail to start with `ImagePullBackOff`, for example on fresh installs (https://github.com/openebs/openebs/pull/4337)

> **Note for upgrades:** `kubectl openebs upgrade` runs Helm with `--reset-then-reuse-values`, so upgraded releases switch to the mirror automatically. Repositories you set explicitly, such as a private registry mirror, are kept. `helm upgrade --reuse-values` keeps the old `quay.io/minio` repositories; use `--reset-then-reuse-values` (Helm 3.14+) instead, or set the repositories explicitly as shown below.

> **Note for users who can't upgrade yet:** Set `loki.minio.image.repository=docker.io/openebs/minio` and `loki.minio.mcImage.repository=docker.io/openebs/mc` on your existing release. The mirror carries the image tags used by v4.3.0 through v4.6.1.

## Replicated Storage (Mayastor)
- Switch Loki's MinIO images in the Mayastor chart to the same OpenEBS mirror. `kubectl mayastor upgrade` moves the MinIO repositories to the mirror only if they are still set to the old `quay.io/minio` defaults, and leaves custom repositories unchanged (https://github.com/openebs/mayastor-extensions/pull/1068)
- The io-engine and control plane are unchanged from v2.12.1.

> **Note:** The Mayastor chart change applies to standalone Mayastor installs. When Mayastor is installed through the OpenEBS chart, its bundled Loki is disabled in favour of the OpenEBS chart's Loki, which is covered under General above.

Refer to the [Mayastor v2.12.2 release notes](https://github.com/openebs/mayastor/releases/tag/v2.12.2) for detailed changes.

## Local Storage
## LVM
- No changes; Local PV LVM remains at v1.10.1.

## ZFS
- Fix the backup and restore pipeline so that a failure on either side is reported and stops the other side. In v2.11.0 and v2.11.1 (OpenEBS v4.6.0 and v4.6.1), a receiver that exited early could leave `zfs send` blocked indefinitely, keeping the `ZFSBackup` in `Init` and blocking later Velero backups. A failed `zfs send` could also be reported as a successful backup. Failed transfers are now marked `Failed` instead of staying in `Init` or being reported as `Done` (https://github.com/openebs/zfs-localpv/pull/777)

> **Note for Velero users:** Failures that were previously reported as `Done` are now reported as `Failed`, so the first backups after upgrading may surface transfers that were already broken.

## Rawfile
This release includes the changes from Local PV Rawfile v0.15.2 and v0.15.3, as v4.6.1 shipped v0.15.1.
- Add a `rawfile-localpv.tls.insecureSkipVerify` Helm value (default `false`) that skips x509 verification when the driver's Kubernetes client talks to the API server, for environments with malformed API server certificates. Only enable it if you understand the security implications (https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/pull/417)
- Add `rawfile-localpv.node.podLabels` and `rawfile-localpv.controller.podLabels` Helm values for Pod labels that are not used as selector labels (https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/pull/416)
- Fix operations such as volume expansion failing on volumes created before storage pools were introduced in v0.13.0 (for example, with OpenEBS v4.4.0). The metadata of these volumes still pointed to the backing file under the old `/data` path; the node plugin now migrates it to the storage pool layout when it starts. If a volume's backing file isn't found in its storage pool, its path is left unchanged and a warning is logged for manual inspection (https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/pull/422)
- Treat StorageClass parameters with empty or null-like values (`""`, `none`, `null`, `nil`) as unset, so the parameter's default applies (https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/pull/413)

## Hostpath
- No changes; Local PV Hostpath remains at v4.6.0.

# New Contributors
- @linkvt made their first contribution in https://github.com/openebs/zfs-localpv/pull/777
- @poblahblahblah made their first contribution in https://github.com/openebs/rawfile-localpv/pull/416
